review_record: owner authorization given in the Claude Code session that prepared this change; no separate reviewer record was produced
approval_basis: Owner-authorized release of the multi-SIMD-group Metal lowering. This approval was written by the author session at the owner's explicit instruction; no independent reviewer session inspected the change, so it does not carry the independent-review basis of earlier approvals under ADR 0052. What the author session did verify, with receipts retained in the session: the Corpus Gate was rebuilt from source and matched 122/122 cases over 169 bound sources for draft open-cake-ir-sm100a-v67-draft; all 120 pre-existing corpus expectations are unchanged and only two new cases were added (metal-rmsnorm-simd-groups-accepted, metal-rmsnorm-simd-group-drift-refused); the emitter's single-SIMD-group output is byte-identical before and after the change across all seven Metal corpus schedules, so every previously released lowering is preserved; and kernels at 2, 4, 8 and 16 SIMD groups were built and checked against the task oracle on an actual Apple M2 device, all passing. Measured on that device, eight groups is 1.46x SLOWER than one group for the 128x1024 RMSNorm shape (pooled medians 14.669us against 10.044us, one group winning 9 of 10 interleaved pairs): this is an opt-in capability for schedules that need a narrower per-lane footprint, not a speedup, and no performance claim is approved here. The cross-group exchange for a narrower non-scalar operand is explicitly refused rather than emitted, and threadgroup memory remains zero for single-group schedules. This approves the Compiler successor only; it approves no Executor release, no framework acceptance and no scientific arm comparison.
